<module id="fixed_point_adder">
    <description>A parameterized fixed-point adder for arithmetic operations with fixed precision.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[N-1:0]">First N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[N-1:0]">Second N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[N-1:0]">N-bit output representing the result of the fixed-point addition.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="Q">Number of fractional bits (precision).</parameter>
        <parameter id="N">Total number of bits, including integer and fractional parts.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <reg id="res" width_description="[N-1:0]">Register to store the result of the addition or subtraction.</reg>
        
        // Determine if the signs of 'a' and 'b' are the same
        <wire id="same_sign">((~a[N-1]) & (~b[N-1])) | ((a[N-1]) & (b[N-1]));</wire>
        
        // Calculate the absolute values of 'a' and 'b'
        <wire id="abs_a">a + {N{(~a[N-1])}};</wire>
        <wire id="abs_b">b + {N{(~b[N-1])}};</wire>
        
        // Perform absolute value addition if the signs are the same
        <assign id="abs_sum">abs_a + abs_b;</assign>
        
        // Perform absolute value subtraction if the signs are different
        <assign id="abs_diff">abs_a > abs_b ? abs_a - abs_b : abs_b - abs_a;</assign>
        
        // Assign the result based on the sign comparison
        <always @(*) begin
            if (same_sign) begin
                res = abs_sum;
                res[N-1] = a[N-1];
            end else begin
                res = abs_diff;
                res[N-1] = ~abs_diff[N-1];
            end
        end
        
        // Output assignment
        <assign id="c">res;</assign>
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Fixed-point adder implementation with parameterization for precision and total bits.</implementation>
</module>
